items.title: Award in Customer Care for Accommodation Establishment Employees
items.description:
This training programme will familiarize employees with the best practices for greeting accommodation establishment guests, providing guest service information, professionally handling any guest request or concern, and practicing effective communication skills to achieve high guest satisfaction.
At the end of this training course the trainee will have been exposed to the following knowledge:
a)	Be conversant with welcoming, greeting, and farewelling accommodation establishment guests.
b)	Be familiar with the provision of guest service information and the handling of guest concerns.
c)	Demonstrate an understanding on the practices of attending guest bedrooms (e.g., handling guest belongings and ‘Do Not Disturb’ cards).
d)	Be conversant in professional grooming and presentation.
e)	Be familiar with the best practices of communication (including briefings) and with high standard customer satisfaction practices.   
f)	Recognize intercultural diversity and demonstrate intercultural awareness.

items.title: Award in Professional Service in Hospitality,  Food and Beverage
items.description:
This qualification is built in line with the National Occupational Standards in relation to hospitality in Malta and successful candidates should be eligible for employment in variety of contexts in food and beverage industry The objectives of this award is to take employees to the next level in their understanding of what it means to provide excellent quality service and offer outstanding service to all customers and guests,  thus improving their effectiveness and the company’s competitiveness in the hospitality industry. The overall objectives of the Award are to engage students in learning that is relevant to their profession and to further develop a range of skills and techniques,  personal skills and attributes necessary for a successful career.
Work and coordinate well as a member of any team; Interact and communicate professionally with customers and guests; Take ownership of his/her career development Understand roles and responsibilities necessary to work in hospitality and catering industries

items.title: Certificate in Events
items.description: Understand various event elements such as food and beverage service,  design and emtertainement. Apply knowledge and skills to effectively communicate with customers and colleagues in a professional manner. Apply basic sales and marketing principles to ensure the success of an event. Follow legal requirements on safety,  health and hygiene Understand basic theories and process of personal events planning.

items.title: BeautyTech MQF Level 3 Certificate in Hairdressing
items.description:
This course aims to provide comprehensive training that includes the underpinning knowledge that is required when performing hairdressing tasks as well as the practical competencies.
Consult their text books to obtain the underpinning knowledge needed to carry out the practical work they will perform; evaluate the information collected; use the knowledge acquired to perform practical tasks correctly; use the interent for research in order to produce assignments and portfolios and gather information and present the knowledge acquired in their own words as assignments The learner will be able to perform all practical hairdressing tasks autonomously,  competently,  safely within acceptable time frames; the learner will be in posession of the underpinning knowledge required to carry our hairdressing tasks Communicate effectively with their superiors,  colleagues and clients; meet and greet clients,  take appointments efficiently personally and by telephone; address visitors to the salon including suppliers,  services providers,  authorities etc; refer clients or visitors to the competent person; carry out consultations in order to obtain information from clients to establish their desires and needs

items.title: Award in Manicure Treatments
items.description:
This course will cover the essential topics  required for a person to work as a beauty therapist safely, effectively and independently. 
It covers theoretical underpinning knowledge required to work safely, as well as practical competences required to work safely and effectively in this industry. The students will be required to further their practical skills on live models at home or in a salon environment. Students may be assigned observational work placements. Theoretical knowledge is assessed through assignments for each unit.
At the end of the module/unit the learner will have been exposed to the following: 

1. Describe skin structure and function
2. List muscles and bones of the hand and arms
3. Name blood and lymph vessels of the hands and arms
4. Draw and describe the structure of the nail 
5. List Contra indications as well as nail diseases and disorders 
6. Knowledge of basic cosmetic chemistry and different types of nail polishes available. 
7. Provide after care advise. At the end of the module/unit the learner will have acquired the following skills: 

1. Carry out client consultation
2. Sanitise hands and nails. 
3. Cut, file, buff, cuticle work, massage and apply nail polish. 
4. Perform a spa manicure and a specialised manicure. 
5. Understand the factors limiting or restricting treatment
6. Provide after care advice At the end of the module/unit the learner will have acquired the responsibility and autonomy to:

1. Consult and keep a detailed record.
2. Identify hand and nail conditions. 
3. Check for contra indications. 
4. Devise a treatment plan. 
5. Perform a manicure. 
6. Give aftercare advice.

items.title: Award in Mathematical Proficiency
items.description:
This programme will consist of online lectures spanning over sixteen weeks, with one lecture a week. It will consist of four modules: a) Number b) Algebra c) Shapes, Space and Measures d) Data Handling.
Topics are scaffolded so that students build on previous knowledge. Both pencil and paper methods as well as calculator methods will be used. Emphasis will be put on how the mathematics learnt is used in daily life and how different methods can be used to arrive at the same answer.
• Understand the structure of the number system and the relationship between numbers.
• Use a variety of calculation procedures (mental methods, pen and paper methods, and assistive technology methods) and associated skills. 
• Understand patterns, sequences, algebraic expressions, formulae, equations, and inequalities. 
• Recognise graphical representations of algebraic functions. 
• Appreciate forms of measurement dealing with angles, length, area, volume, capacity, mass, and time. 
• Identify the properties of lines, segments, parallel lines, perpendicular lines, transversals, angles, 2D and 3D shapes.
• Draw the construction of angles, lines, triangles, circles, others polygons and loci in 2D. 
• Understand position and movement of shapes in a plane. 
• Read measures of central tendency, measures of dispersion and graphical representation of data. 
• Appreciate the probabilities associated with certain, uncertain and impossible events. • Understand and appreciate the place and purpose of Mathematics in society and apply mathematical concepts to situations arising in their own lives.
• Apply mathematical knowledge and understanding to solve problems.
• Think and communicate mathematically - precisely, logically and creatively.
• Develop a positive attitude to Mathematics, including confidence and perseverance.
• Develop an ability to work independently and co-operatively when doing Mathematics.
• Appreciate the interdependence of the different branches of Mathematics.
• Acquire a secure foundation for the further study of Mathematics.
• Use Mathematics across the curriculum and make efficient, creative, and effective use of appropriate technology in Mathematics

items.title: Award in Housekeeping - Clean it up!
items.description:
This course provides information on how to provide the appropriate housekeeping service to guests. The objective is to provide learners with the basics of housekeeping,  including: identifying different types of accommodation,  parts therein,  and respective service expected; language skills needed; and security and safety issues common in the field. It is true that it is only through hands-on experience and practise that staff can learn to reach the time and quality targets set,  but the course prepares students for what to expect.
Adapt one’s own experiences as a client of the industry to improve knowledge and skills. Assess strengths and areas for personal development with regards to the skills and knowledge needed to fulfil job role requirements. Fill in forms as per establishment’s standards. Communicate with clients according to organisational guidelines – the focus being functional language such as greetings and inquiring on one’s needs.

items.title: VET Award for Care Workers for the Elderly

items.title: MQF Level 3 Award in Placement in Commercial Multi-Disciplinary Production
items.description:

It will be available to all students through regular multi-disciplinary productions that the College produces or by other production houses approved by the College. The artistic director will ensure parity

2. Mental health first aid.

3. Depression.

4. Anxiety Problems.

5. Psychosis.

6. Substance use problems.

7. First aid for suicidal thoughts.

8. First aid for non-suicidal self-injury.

9. First aid for panic attacks.

10. First aid following a traumatic event.

11. First aid for severe psychotic states.

12. First aid for severe effects of alcohol use.

13. First aid for severe effects from drug use.

14. First aid for aggressive behaviors.

2. Be able to distinguish between different mental health problems vis a vis through understanding of the idiosyncratic symptoms of various mental health problems.

3. Adopt to approaching, assessing, assisting and supporting a person who is developing a mental health problem or is in a mental health crisis.

4. Be able to prudently listen to a person who is suffering from a mental health problem or crisis in a non-judgmental manner.

6. Be well-versed enough in order to suggest the most adequate form of professional help for a person who is developing a mental health problem, or is in a crisis.

7. Be able to sensitively encourage the family members and friends of a person suffering from a mental health problem to provide continual support. 1. Understand the fundamental underpinnings of mental health.

10. Be able to sensitively encourage the family members and friends of a person suffering from a mental health problem to provide continual support.

11. Be able to perform the recovery position.

items.title: Award in Manual Handling
items.description:
Manual handling, also known as manual tasks, is any activity requiring effort to lift, move, push, pull, carry or hold any object, including a person.
Poor manual handling practice is one of the most common causes of injury in the health care industry. These injuries are frequently severe and cannot always be completely treated, leading to chronic problems.

This Award has been created specifically for the needs of workers in the Health Care industry and will teach learners how to safely identify, plan and perform manual handling tasks to assist in maintaining an injury-free workplace.
a)	Look after their own back and that of patients / residents 
b)	Promote compliance with relevant regulations and guidelines
c)	Assess personal risks for patients / residents and minimise workplace risks
d)	Use the right technique for moving and handling tasks
e)	Safely move people with and without the use of specialist equipment
f)	Move and handle people in a way that requires the least amount of effort
g)	Move and handle people in a way that provides greater comfort and dignity to the patient or resident The learner will be able to:
a)	Look after their own back and that of patients / residents
b)	Use all adequate and appropriate handling equipment in a safe and effective manner
c)	Apply principles of good practice when using equipment for patient handling
d)	Safely move people with and without the use of specialist equipment
e)	Carry out moving, handling, and early ambulation according to the mobility assessment plan. 
f)	Move and handle people in a way that requires the least amount of effort
g)	Move and handle people in a way that provides greater comfort and dignity to the patient or resident a)	Understand manual handling legislation as it applies to Healthcare
b)	Understand the law and legislation associated with patient moving and handling 
c)	Understand how to reduce negligence, accidents and incidents to patients, service users, and visitors

e)	Understand patient handling needs and movement patterns
f)	Understand principles of patient risk assessment & mobility assessment plans

items.title: Award in Safe, Hygienic and Secure Working Environments in Hospitality

The Airlines Cabin Crew Training Course provides an understanding of the travel history,  describes the travel professional's role in the airlines industry,  the role of technology and the importance of exceeding customer expectations. Fundamental skills and competencies linked to airlines safety and emergency procedures and regulations,  which are the core aspect underlying this course,  are to be given prominence,  as is apparent in the course programme (vide module 2). In addition,  air transport and flight operations,  airports regulations,  Medical emergencies on-board aircraft,  airlines catering and duty free services shall also be addressed as essential factors. This course also provides details on how to apply for the Cabin Crew job (Preparation of Resume and Grooming),  proceed and excel to start a career. This is a vocational training course which follows the parameters established by IATA in accordance with the Aviation Regulations. Upon completion of the course,  applicants will be well versed in the nature and the tasks the Cabin Crew job entails. However,  it is the airlines’ priority whether to accept a job application or not.
